trails.title: "The Original Her"
trails.description: Beyond the spinning wheel, dust spins into a single thread.

content.text:
Classification: Top Secret
From: Zeno Headquarters
To: Zeno Branches

Research confirms that the truth behind the "Storm" is very likely tied to a high-value target known as "Urd." Our primary objective is to locate and make contact with this individual—note: we are seeking the "original her," prior to any influence from the "Storm." The identity of any presently existing individual holds no research value.

High command has established a facility known as the Loop Laboratory along the Don River, codename: "Amber Room." Its existence is classified at the highest level and is to be exempt from external inquiry of any kind. The Loop Laboratory has achieved structural immunity to the "Storm." Per orders, "deserters" have been transferred to the facility to undergo arcane experiments. All procedures are to be directed, documented, and overseen by our personnel only.

All branches are hereby notified of the following resource allocations:
...

Reminder: The Loop Laboratory is of the highest-priority. Any intelligence concerning the target Urd must be reported immediately.

——End of Telegram——

items.text: Mining Area, Chukotka

items.speaker: Hush Squad Commander
items.text: Marguerite!

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Hmm?

items.speaker: Hush Squad Commander
items.text: Explain what you're doing out here.
The year is 1987, just after the second "Storm."
A cold wind sweeps across the Siberian ice fields, lifting snow from the frozen ground and carrying it far away.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Nothing.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: One of them, a girl, has the same name as me.
She wipes away the writing left in the snow.

items.speaker: Hush Squad Commander
items.text: Have you forgotten the Hush Squad's number-one rule? No communication with mission targets!

items.speaker: Hush Squad Commander
items.text: When the LT assigned you to my squad, he said you had the right stuff to be an excellent Hush Trooper.

items.speaker: Hush Squad Commander
items.text: Said you could spot a target in a ghillie suit from two kilometers away.

items.speaker: Hush Squad Commander
items.text: More importantly, he said you were smart. So be smart, and don't meddle in things that aren't your concern, understand?

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Mm-hmm.

items.speaker: Hush Squad Commander
items.text: Break's over. Let's move.
Marguerite lifts her rifle and trudges behind her commander into the blistering wind. At last, they arrive at the transport vehicle.

items.speaker: Hush Squad Commander
items.text: What's going on? Why aren't we moving?

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: It's the engine. Not even our warming incantation can manage against this cold.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: We might have to stop and spend the night here.
The subordinate reports, shivering.

items.speaker: Hush Squad Commander
items.text: Unacceptable!

items.speaker: Hush Squad Commander
items.text: We're still at least three days from the Loop Laboratory's relay station. We can't afford to lose another. We have to get these transfers done on schedule.

items.speaker: Hush Squad Commander
items.text: Or there's no guarantee we'll have enough time to take shelter when the "Storm" hits.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: But I think the deserters need some time to rest as well. Most of them have fallen ill.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: If we keep going like this, they might not make it to the destination.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: I think they could use some sleep and proper medica—

items.speaker: Hush Squad Commander
items.text: That is above your pay grade, trooper. We were ordered to transfer these deserters dead or alive.
Their commander snaps at her before she can finish.

items.speaker: Hush Squad Commander
items.text: Marguerite, go fix the engine.

items.speaker: Hush Squad Commander
items.text: I'll contact Command to confirm the location of our nearest post. I want this convoy burning rubber by the end of the hour. Understood?

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Yes, ma'am.
Without a word, Marguerite inspects the broken engine. Nearby, Larisa looks worried.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: *sigh* Sure is cold up near the mines, huh?

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: If I hadn't joined Zeno, I'd probably be sitting in a warm classroom right now.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: *sigh* I wonder what university life is like.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Don't dream too much. University can be just as strange as anywhere else.
The distant young woman keeps her gaze lowered.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Back in 1999, I was auditing a philosophy class at Cambridge, just to watch some bird-headed professor declare out-of-the-blue that teaching philosophy was an absurd profession.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: He quit and joined the Laplace Scientific Computing Center.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: Haha, that's a good one—going to university in 1999. How old would you have been? 13? 14?

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: How'd a prodigy like you end up stuck in the Hush Squad?

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Could be I just enjoy the work. It's calming.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Could be that I hope someday to find my purpose here.
Marguerite slams the hood shut, and the engine roars to life.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: Yeah, sure, if walking across an ice field at forty below isn't calming, I don't know what is.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Study your target, predict their movement, track them down, and then ...
She mimics firing a gun with her hand.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: That's what makes you calm? You've got to be joking.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Yeah, just joking.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: *sigh* All I wanted was to join the Flying Witches.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Then why are you here, stealing intel and carrying out assassinations?

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: The lieutenant promised that the Hush Squad comes with a generous salary and death benefits.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: You know, at the time, my mom was sick.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: And then, the "Storm" struck. Guess I didn't really need the money in the end.
A short, dry laugh escapes her lips, but Marguerite doesn't match it.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: Do you have any idea what this Loop Laboratory does, Marguerite?

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: We've transferred over a hundred deserters there since summer, but I've never seen any of them come back out.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: Probably none of my business. I once helped with a Zeno recruitment drive in a war zone. I saw a lot of things there.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: Those soldiers, they lost everything in the war. They only joined Zeno because they heard they'd get proper meals, not exactly what I'd call willing recruits.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: These arcanist deserters we've been moving, they just weren't ready to face death yet.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: Marguerite, I'm telling you this because I trust you.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: I know what it does.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: Huh? What do you mean?

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: The Loop Laboratory.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: It has another name: the Amber Room.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: At the end of the battle in 1999, a massive number of soldiers were lost to the "Storm." It was a devastating blow to Zeno's military strength.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: From then on, the higher-ups have been trying to find a woman named Urd, or to be exact, the woman she was before being reversed by the "Storm."

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: That's why they built the Loop Laboratory near the Don River. It's a facility that can resist the "Storm."

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: The "deserters" aren't being transferred there for any ordinary training or dry runs.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: The things they do to the deserters' bodies involve unprecedented arcane powers related to the "Storm" itself.
Before she realizes it, the listener's back is damp with cold sweat.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: I-I don't think I understand. How do you know all this?

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: I read the classified files sealed in Warehouse 0 at headquarters.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: You went into Warehouse 0?! They could have shot you just for stepping in there! Tell me you're just joking!

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: You got me again.
Larisa breathes out a sigh of relief.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: I've got another joke: sometimes I eavesdrop on Zeno's encrypted telegrams, just for fun.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: The problem is, the encryption patterns are so repetitive that cracking them's become boring.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: *sigh* I honestly can't tell which of your jokes is more disturbing.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: The European branches have been bending over backwards to look for the original copies of The Tome of Mercury and The Path to Truth.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: But to find their owners—the famous Cavendish family of alchemists, we'll need the "Storm" to take us further back in time.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Meanwhile, a squad from the Buenos Aires branch has been searching for a rare arcane metal, likely a special silver ore from Mexico's Vale of Tears.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: And the Egypt branch has sent Roar Lion Tails and Sacred Scarab Wings to the Loop Laboratory in droves.
Larisa searches for some clear meaning to what she's hearing.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: But what does all this mean? What are they trying to achieve?

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: I'm not sure, but one thing's for certain: it's all connected to the Loop Laboratory's arcane experiments.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: To find the truth behind the "Storm."

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: All those experiments ... They must have found something, right?

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: No, Larisa, not even close.
Her face is expressionless, emotionless, almost blank.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: All signs point to a goal coveted by every alchemist, a feat humanity has never succeeded in achieving.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: It's hardly surprising they're still groping in the dark, looking for a key object, a step, or more likely, a person.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: And these so-called "deserters"? Fodder. Even if they survive the experiments, they'll just be thrown out to face the next "Storm."

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: No way.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: I probably shouldn't ask, Marguerite, but, what did you mean by "so-called"?
Marguerite seizes on the question, reading her comrade's nerves with her eyes.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: You've guessed already, haven't you?

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: Guessed what? What are you trying to say?

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: That these poor wretches are anything but "deserters."

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Apparently, they were unfortunate enough to meet the experiment criteria, so Zeno fabricated their desertion charges and had them sent to the laboratory.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: So, you know the truth. What are you going to do?
She has her on the edge, precisely where she wants her to be, but it isn't quite enough yet to push her over.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: *deep breath* I-I don't know. I need some time to think.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: In any case, I think I'll take some time to give the deserters. I mean, whatever I mean, I'll give them some medication so they can at least survive the journey there.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: I know you won't stop me, Marguerite.
Marguerite shrugs.
The Hush Trooper unlocks the truck. Inside, thin, sickly teenagers huddle together for warmth.

items.speaker: Deserter I
items.text: L-Larisa, will we be there soon?

items.speaker: Deserter II
items.text: Everyone's in bad shape, but we've agreed among ourselves we don't want to cause you any more trouble, really.

items.speaker: Deserter II
items.text: Fomá and Stepán are asleep now. I just hope their fever subsides.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: *sigh* Don't worry. We'll reach our destination in just a few days. There'll be a warm place to stay and plenty of soup and bread.

items.speaker: Hush Trooper
items.text: Sílviya, could you help hand out these antipyretics to anyone who needs them?

items.speaker: Deserter II
items.text: Oh, of course. We really can't thank you enough, Larisa.
Footsteps crunch behind her, carried by the whipping wind.

items.speaker: Hush Squad Commander
items.text: Alright, we just made contact with the Foundation's Far East branch and—

items.speaker: Hush Squad Commander
items.text: Larisa! Marguerite! What the hell are you doing?

items.speaker: Hush Squad Commander
items.text: Didn't I say these deserters weren't your concern?
Hallway, Laplace
A researcher stands before a derelict-looking office and knocks on the door.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Mr. Ludwig, were you looking for me?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I know I'm a little early, but if I had waited any longer, I would have been caught up by my bothersome fellow researchers again.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Are you in there?
No answer comes. Faint burn marks on the door hint at a severe fire months ago.
Suddenly, the sound of lab equipment crashing echoes from inside.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Umm, Mr. Ludwig?
